Complete a product and list factor pairs

question: A rectangular floor measures \(a\) feet by \(b\) feet, where \(a\) and \(b\) are positive integers with \(b\gt a.\) An artist paints a rectangle on the floor with the sides of the rectangle parallel to the sides of the floor. The unpainted part of the floor forms a border of width \(1\) foot around the painted rectangle and occupies half the area of the entire floor. How many possibilities are there for the ordered pair \((a,b)?\)
solution:
A one-foot border removes two feet from each dimension, so the painted rectangle measures \(a-2\) by \(b-2\). Both dimensions must be positive, hence \(b>a>2\).

The painted and unpainted regions each occupy half the floor, so
\[
(a-2)(b-2)=\frac{ab}{2}.
\]
We want to use the integer conditions, so rewrite this equation as a fixed product:
\[
\begin{aligned}
ab-4a-4b+8&=0,\\
ab-4a-4b+16&=8,\\
(a-4)(b-4)&=8.
\end{aligned}
\]
Since \(a\) and \(b\) are integers with \(b>a>2\), we have \(b\ge4\). Thus \(b-4\ge0\); the nonzero positive product forces both \(b-4\) and \(a-4\) to be positive. Also, \(a-4<b-4\).

The increasing positive factor pairs of \(8\) are exactly \((1,8)\) and \((2,4)\). They give
\[
(a,b)=(5,12)\quad\text{or}\quad(6,8).
\]
For these pairs, the painted areas are \(3\cdot10=30\) and \(4\cdot6=24\), respectively, half the corresponding floor areas \(60\) and \(48\). Both satisfy \(b>a\), and the factor-pair list is exhaustive. Therefore there are \(\boxed{2}\) possibilities, choice \(\text{B}\).

solutionMethods.explanation:
The painted rectangle has dimensions \(a-2\) and \(b-2\), with \(b>a>2\). Its fraction of the floor's area is therefore
\[
\frac{a-2}{a}\cdot\frac{b-2}{b}=\frac12.
\]
Bounding this fraction will leave very few possibilities for the integer \(a\).

If \(a\le4\), then \((a-2)/a\le1/2\). Since \(0<(b-2)/b<1\), their product would be less than \(1/2\), which is impossible. Hence \(a\ge5\).

If \(a\ge7\), then \(b>a\) implies that both retained side fractions are at least \(5/7\). The painted area fraction would then be at least
\[
\left(\frac57\right)^2=\frac{25}{49}>\frac12,
\]
again impossible. Thus \(a\le6\), leaving only \(a=5\) and \(a=6\).

For \(a=5\), the area equation becomes
\[
3(b-2)=\frac{5b}{2},
\]
so \(6b-12=5b\) and \(b=12\).

For \(a=6\), it becomes
\[
4(b-2)=3b,
\]
so \(b=8\).

Both pairs have positive painted dimensions and satisfy \(b>a\). Their painted areas, \(30\) and \(24\), are half their floor areas, \(60\) and \(48\). The bounds exclude every other integer \(a\), so there are exactly \(\boxed{2}\) pairs, choice \(\text{B}\).
